title: Scaling Laws and Compute Budgets
summary: Loss falls predictably, as a power law, when you add parameters, data and compute. This lesson turns that regularity into a planning tool: estimate the compute of a run with C ≈ 6ND, split a budget between model size and tokens, and decide when to train a smaller model for longer.
objectives: Read a power law on a log-log plot and compute how much loss falls when a model or dataset grows
Evaluate the Chinchilla loss formula L(N, D) = E + A/N^α + B/D^β and explain each term
Derive C ≈ 6ND and convert a training run into FLOPs, GPU-days and dollars
Find the compute-optimal model size and token count for a budget using the 20-tokens-per-parameter rule
Explain why production models are often trained far past the compute-optimal point
prerequisites: You should know the pretraining objective and the idea of tokens per parameter ([Pretraining Data](/learn/training-and-adaptation/pretraining-data)), and roughly how parameters are counted in a transformer ([The Transformer Block](/learn/model-foundations/transformer-block)). Comfort with logarithms and exponents helps; they are reviewed where used.
